name: Asset classification — Hub vs DataCore divergence
description: Explains why the same asset can show as one type in the Hub (e.g. COMPUTER) and a different type in DataCore (e.g. MOBILE). Both call the SAME discovery-recognition-api (Fing wrapper) — but the Hub only hits the basic devrecog endpoint, while DataCore additionally calls the catalog endpoint (richer brand/model/os/sw data). The richer data lets DataCore reassign the LegacyAssetType, and DataCore applies a second exclusion check after reconciliation.

annotations.text: gRPC wrapper over Fing. Returns type, model, brand, os-name, recogtype. See recognition-flow for detail.

Spring bean inside the processor (libs/recognition). Makes an outbound gRPC call to discovery-recognition-api (Fing) using the devrecog endpoint. LECDataCore/libs/recognition/.../ReactiveGrpcDeviceRecognitionService.java

Spring bean inside the processor (libs/recognition). Outbound gRPC call to discovery-recognition-api (Fing) catalog endpoint — richer payload (brand/model/os/sw/monitor). Cached in-memory via DefaultCachedReactiveBulkCatalogLookupService. LECDataCore/libs/recognition/.../ReactiveCatalogLookupService.java

Java class. Runs AFTER reconciliation. Reads the FINAL LegacyAssetType from asset.proto.core.type.lsId and emits ExcludedAssetTypeException if excluded. LECDataCore/libs/reconciliation/.../ExcludedAssetTypeReconciliationPostProcessor.java

nodes.text:
HUB EXCLUSION CHECK = doble match contra cada GlobalExclusion de tipo AssetType:
  1) enum:   device.AssetType == MapExclusionStringToAssetType(excl.Exclusion)
             (switch limitado: windows | linux | apple mac | monitor | unknown → null si no)
  2) string: device.LsTypeName.CaseInsensitiveEquals(excl.Exclusion)   ← fallback

Basta con que UNO de los dos haga match (y que el sensor esté en el alcance).

Entonces para excluir 'Mobile' funcionaría — SI Fing hubiera devuelto LsTypeName='Mobile'. En el caso real Fing devolvió 'Computer', así que ningún match dispara.

Lansweeper.IT/.../GlobalExclusions/ExclusionHelper.cs
  MarkDeviceWithExcludedAssetTypeAsExcludedToAvoidSync()

MISMO SERVICIO, ENDPOINT DISTINTO
Tanto Hub como DataCore llaman a la MISMA discovery-recognition-api (wrapper de Fing).
La diferencia:
  • Hub usa endpoint 'devrecog' → type básico desde OS name
  • DataCore llama TAMBIÉN al endpoint catalog → trae brand/model/os/sw/monitor

Con esos datos extra, el mapper de DataCore puede traducir model='iPhone' → LegacyAssetType.IPHONE.
Resultado: Hub almacena type='Computer' (Fing devrecog devolvió eso), DataCore escribe type='iPhone' en el proto.

RECONCILIATION = rule-based, NOT a single key.
Every delta-merge runs all enabled rules to build CorrFields. EntityKey = (siteId, UUID).

Rules include:
  • MacAddressRule — confidence 80+ on MAC overlap
  • IpAddressRule
  • ImeiRule (Intune)
  • ADUserUPNRule, AD SID rules

See LECDataCore/docs/new-reconciliation-analysis.md

DC EXCLUSION = FINAL TYPE check
Reads asset.proto.core.type.lsId AFTER catalog enrichment, then calls scanning-config gRPC getExcludedAssetTypes(siteId, sourceId) and emits ExcludedAssetTypeException if matched.

Exception stops the pipeline → asset NOT synced downstream (no asset.event emitted).

EL CASO DEL USUARIO — site con exclusión 'Mobile', mismo asset (mac=1) escaneado por CDR (A) y luego Deep (B):

A → Hub: Fing devuelve LsTypeName='Computer' → device.LsTypeName='Computer' → ExclusionHelper compara contra 'Mobile' (enum y string) → ningún match → PASA → SyncerAPI
  → DataCore: first time, no candidates → Recognition + Catalog (modelo → iPhone) → proto.core.type=IPHONE → exclusion postprocessor: IPHONE ∈ excluded → ExcludedAssetTypeException → NOT synced

B → Hub: igual (Fing → 'Computer') → PASA
  → DataCore: MacAddressRule matches A's entity → reconcile to master → master rebuilt → catalog re-applied → type=IPHONE → excluded → NOT synced

La contradicción que veías NO es real: Hub y DataCore usan FUENTES DISTINTAS. Recognition (Fing) ≠ Catalog. El Hub podría excluir 'Mobile' si Fing devolviera ese LsTypeName, pero no es el caso. El catálogo de DataCore sí lo identifica y por eso la exclusión final dispara allí.

RESUMEN HUB vs DATACORE
              Hub                      DataCore
Fing endpoint devrecog (básico)         devrecog + catalog (rico)
Datos input   OS name → type           OS + brand + model + sw + monitor
Mapping LS    5 strings (limitado)     LegacyAssetType completo
Exclusión     string == LsTypeName     lsId ∈ scanning-config set
Cuándo        antes de SyncerAPI       después de reconcile
Si excluye    device.Status=Excluded   ExcludedAssetTypeException → no sync
